name: APT9
affiliation_detail:
Mandiant assesses APT9 as "a freelancer group with some nation-state sponsorship, possibly China."
ASERT's tracking of the group as "Group 27" in the Myanmar watering hole campaign is consistent with Chinese state interests (Belt and Road monitoring, election intelligence) but does not confirm direct government control.
No DOJ indictment or formal government attribution to a specific buereau or unit has been published.
description:
APT9 is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group assessed by Google TI as a "freelancer group with some nation-state sponsorship." The group conducts intellectual property theft, historically with a strong focus on the pharmaceuticals and biotechnology industries, as well as construction, engineering, aerospace, and defense. (Google TI)
APT9 is one of the less publicly documented Chinese APT groups. Limited information comes from Mandiant's brief public description and ASERT/Arbor Networks' "Seven Pointed Dagger" 2015 research on the Group 27 cluster, which targeted several Myanmar government websites during the 2015 elections using watering hole attacks. 
In September 2015, Unit 42, in their research on ‘3102’ trojan targeting US and EU entites, noted suspected relationship between the payload observed and the payload used in a watering hole attack on Myanmar presidential website in 2015.  Furthermote, Unit 42 noted of "ties between the C2 infrastructure and individuals in China active in online hacking forums that claim to work in Trojan development."

campaigns.name: Myanmar Election Watering Hole (Seven Pointed Dagger)
campaigns.description: ASERT discovered watering hole attacks on official Myanmar government websites, including the Union Election Commission (UEC), timed to the November 2015 general elections. The Group 27 cluster used PlugX malware delivered via compromised election information pages. Further investigation uncovered a cluster of seven malware families ("Seven Pointed Dagger"): two PlugX variants, two Trochilus RAT variants, one 9002 RAT (3102 variant), one EvilGrab RAT, and one unidentified sample. The campaign indicated interest in Myanmar's Special Economic Zones and election outcomes. The group continued operating through the same compromised websites even after public disclosure by Cisco Talos and Arbor Networks.

campaigns.name: Biotechnology / Pharmaceutical IP Theft
campaigns.description: Mandiant observed APT9 targeting multiple organizations in the pharmaceuticals and biotechnology industries. In at least one case, the group was simultaneously present in two biotech companies and is assessed to have leveraged a trusted business relationship between the two firms to pivot from one to the other. This is one of the earliest documented examples of the trusted-relationship initial access technique in the Chinese APT context. Specific timeframes and victim identities have not been publicly disclosed.
